23/G.goal: Explain why XR systems are interactive systems and how user-centric, human-factors principles guide their design for lay users.
23/G.achieves: Prepares the learner to incorporate human factors and user-centered design into later understanding, development, and evaluation of XR systems.

23/O1.goal: Explain why XR systems should be treated as interactive systems and how the disappearing-technology ideal supports presence and design for lay users.
23/O1.achieves: Gives the learner a rationale for making XR technology unobtrusive and usable by non-experts before applying human-factors design in later XR development.

23/O2.goal: Describe the human-centered design framework for interactive XR systems by connecting the user-centric approach, HCI, and human factors to user characteristics.
23/O2.achieves: Enables the learner to consider user characteristics and human factors when designing or evaluating XR interfaces in the course case study.
